name: The Reel Deal Deck
positioning: The first fly-fishing deck an angler would be proud to own. Original hand-drawn art, printed on genuine Bicycle stock, with a portion of every deck going to Trout Unlimited.

founders.name: Ken Fry
founders.bio: Lifelong entrepreneur of more than thirty years, fifth-generation Idaho farmer, and the avid amateur angler who went looking for fly-fishing flashcards, came up empty-handed, and set about making the set he could not buy.

founders.name: Audrey Fry
founders.bio: Sixth-generation Idaho farmer and an entrepreneurship graduate of Loyola Marymount University's College of Business Administration, December 2025. Handles design direction, brand and community — and is the reason the drawings became a deck instead of a folder on a laptop.

A further bonus card ships in the deck and is deliberately not mentioned in any public copy — see data/flies.json, the entry flagged bonus:true.
product.originNote: Printed by The United States Playing Card Company. Drawn, packed and shipped by Ken and Audrey in Eagle, Idaho. This is the one claim on the site that is true end to end, and /story/ is where it is made.

blog.name: The Virtual Guide

blog.authorNote: TODO-CONFIRM: articles are attributed to the brand, not a named person. If Ken wants a byline (recommended — it is a real expertise signal for both Google and AI answer engines), add him here and to the Person schema.

social.emailNote: CONFIGURATION ONLY — do not render this into a page. It was in the footer partial, so it shipped on all 98 pages, plus the Organization JSON-LD on six more; the spam started within days of the site going public. Harvesters read markup, comments and structured data alike. Every route to it is now /contact/, which posts to netlify/functions/contact.mjs; the function reads SUPPORT_EMAIL from the environment and is the only thing that knows the address. If you need a mailto: again, you do not — add a topic to the contact form instead.

placeholders.note: Checkout is Shopify-hosted and lives at site.shop.url. Everything else that collects an address or an email on this site is still a local-storage stub and says so on the page. See docs/COMMERCE.md.

motto: The finest gift to fellow anglers is the fish you gently release.

voice.source: Transcribed verbatim from the info card printed in the deck (Fly_deck_faces_v8 #56). Use these words; do not paraphrase them into marketing-speak.
voice.intro: We're Ken and Audrey, a father-daughter team of multigenerational Idaho farmers and entrepreneurs.
voice.why: And as passionate fly anglers, we are dedicated to catch-and-release fishing and protecting our headwaters and trout habitats. That's why we created The Reel Deal Deck — exquisite hand-drawn playing cards that teach while you play.
voice.hope: We hope this deck sparks joy, conversation, and a deeper love for the sport.
voice.signoff: Thank you for your support. Tight lines!
voice.shortLine: Hand-drawn playing cards that teach while you play.
voice.note: The printed card says 'multigenerational Idaho farmers' of the pair. All three facts behind that are now confirmed by Ken and Audrey: the surname is Fry (it is also in brand.legalName, Homer Fry Ranch, LLC), Ken is the fifth generation and Audrey the sixth. Use the full names in schema, press boilerplate and bylines; first names alone are correct in the site's own voice.
voice.register: How the site itself should sound, as distinct from voice.intro/why/hope/signoff, which are printed-card text and must be quoted verbatim. Write as Ken and Audrey, not about them: 'we made', 'we would rather', never 'Ken and Audrey decided' on a page they are speaking on. Warm, plain and a little wry — a father and daughter showing you a thing they made, not a brand announcing a product. Specific over grand, and never a claim we cannot back. No exclamation marks and no emoji: that is their Instagram voice, and it does not survive the move to a page someone is reading to decide whether to spend $19.95. Third person is still right in schema, alt text, press boilerplate and product facts ('signed by Ken and Audrey').

cardCraft.suits: A two-color deck: green replaces red on hearts and diamonds, bark brown replaces black on spades and clubs — drawn from the tuck box and card back.
cardCraft.backDesign: An engraved green border framing two rising trout and an angler on the river.
cardCraft.jokers: Two jokers carry a trout-in-a-jester's-cap mark instead of a rank: the Egg and the San Juan Worm.
cardCraft.infoCard: A 56th card carries Ken and Audrey's note, the site address and the Trout Unlimited Business mark.
cardCraft.eachCard: Every card shows the rank and suit, the fly's name, its category, the hand-drawn fly itself, a plain-English note on what it imitates, and the hook sizes it is usually tied in.
cardCraft.printer: The United States Playing Card Company

story.note: Ken and Audrey's own account, condensed from their Kickstarter campaign page. Full transcript and the rules for writing in this voice: docs/VOICE-SOURCE.md. Do not add a beat that is not sourced there. NOTE the campaign says they work 'with experienced graphic designers in Adobe Illustrator' — see story.artNote.
story.hook: Fly fishing is full of beauty, tradition and endless learning. It is also full of hundreds of flies, each with its own name, purpose and history — exciting, and a little overwhelming even for experienced anglers.
story.looking: Ken fishes with friends who can talk patterns, techniques and history all afternoon, and some of the finer details went over his head. He went looking for a set of fly-fishing flashcards to fix that, and could not even find one.
story.twist: So he thought: why not make his own? And then came the twist — why not make them double as playing cards?
story.belief: We think a product can do more than sell. It can teach, start a conversation, bring people together, and talk somebody into an afternoon outside.
story.spirit: It is a small product with a big spirit behind it.
goal: special enough to leave on a coffee table, in a cabin or in a gear bag
story.forWhom: For anglers of every level, for the friend hunting a gift that feels personal, and for anyone who likes the art and the culture as much as the fishing.
story.thanks: We are so glad you are here.
story.artNote: The cards are original and drawn by hand, and they were NOT drawn by Ken — a designer drew them. The site said otherwise in six places and every one has been corrected. 'Hand-drawn', 'original', 'not photographed' and 'drawn one at a time' all remain true and are load-bearing claims; what was false was attributing them to Ken. His part is that he went looking for a set, could not buy one, and had it made. /story/ deliberately does not go further than that.
story.question: Why is there no easy, enjoyable way to learn the names and varieties of flies?
story.proof: The cards have already made Ken a more knowledgeable angler, which was the only proof the idea worked for a long time.

shop.note: Where every "buy" link on the site points, resolved once by orderState() in src/templates/_blocks.mjs. Checkout is hosted on Shopify, so `url` is the only place the storefront is named. Leave it empty and every CTA falls back to `fallback` — the on-site pricing panel — so the site is never broken while the store is being set up. Never paste a store URL into a page.
shop.urlNote: Set 2026-10-12. The PRODUCT page, not the store root: a visitor who has already read the deck page and pressed Order should land on the thing they can buy, not a storefront they have to navigate. Verified 200. Changing this repoints every order CTA on the site in one move; nothing else names the store.
shop.headline: The Reel Deal Deck is ready to order.
shop.sub: 54 hand-drawn flies on genuine Bicycle stock, $19.95 a deck, with a contribution to Trout Unlimited from every one of them. Shipping is on us from two decks up.
shop.accountUrlNote: Set 2026-10-06, re-pointed 2026-10-12. It carries ?return_url=/pages/wholesale ON PURPOSE. Bare /account 302s to Shopify's HOSTED dashboard on shopify.com, which greets a trade buyer with a “Shop now” card for the RETAIL deck — that page is Shopify's, not the theme's, and the card cannot be re-pointed. Verified chain: /account/login?return_url=%2Fpages%2Fwholesale → /customer_authentication/login?return_to=%2Fpages%2Fwholesale → OAuth → /pages/wholesale, so a signed-in wholesaler lands on their ordering page and never sees the dashboard. Every link that uses this is a wholesale link; there is no retail account link on the site. Originally: /account 302s to the Shopify account portal. Deliberately the shop subdomain rather than https://shopify.com/76483067994/account, which is where it redirects — that numeric id is Shopify's and can change, and a link on our own domain does not read as a phishing hop to a shop owner. The store runs NEW_CUSTOMER_ACCOUNTS, so signing in is an emailed code. The signup collects no password: Shopify's current customer accounts sign in with an emailed code, which is what the apply form and the function assume. Do not switch the store to classic accounts. While this is empty the gate at /wholesale/ offers an email address instead of a dead login link; wholesaleState() in src/templates/_blocks.mjs makes that choice once.

pricing.note: The one source of pricing truth. src/pages/deck.mjs and src/pages/wholesale.html both read it; the Product JSON-LD offer is built from it. Three units, and they nest: a brick is twelve decks, a master case is twelve bricks.

retail.note: One deck is $19.95 plus $6.95 shipping. Two or more decks are $19.95 each and shipping is free. There is no quantity discount at retail — the saving is the shipping.

wholesale.note: Wholesale is per-deck pricing from a Shopify B2B CATALOG attached to a B2B market; the market matches on the company LOCATION that netlify/functions/wholesale-apply.mjs creates. Nothing here gates it and nothing here is rendered: /wholesale/ is a gate page carrying no trade information. The ORDERABLE UNIT and the quantity rules live in the catalog, not in this file and not in the product catalogue — minimum 24 decks, in increments of 12, so a shop can order two bricks, three, or five. The old model made the bundles themselves the products, which could only ever sell even numbers of bricks.

account.note: The wholesale account flow. /wholesale/apply/ posts to the Netlify function in netlify/functions/, which creates a B2B COMPANY — company, location and first contact in one Admin call — and stores the resale permit as a company metafield. Trade pricing is the catalog, reached through the B2B market the location matches. There is no `wholesale` tag any more and no automatic discount: the tag granted nothing once the catalog existed. Setup runbook: docs/WHOLESALE-ACCOUNTS.md.
account.liveNote: The master switch for the application form. FALSE while the site is on GitHub Pages, where /api/wholesale-apply is a 404 and the form has nowhere to post: the page then shows the email route instead of a form that would fail and blame the applicant's connection. Set true the day the site moves to Netlify AND the Shopify environment variables are set — not before, and not one without the other. Nothing else needs changing.
account.autoApproveNote: Approved on signup. REVIEW_ONLY=1 no longer withholds pricing: on a non-Plus plan a catalog attaches to a MARKET and a market matches a location's address, so one company cannot be held back from a market it matches. Direct catalog-to-company assignment, which would allow it, is Plus only. REVIEW_ONLY now only marks the company note. If applications must genuinely be reviewed before pricing, close the form — set live to false — and take them by email.

wholesale.tiersNote: Quantity price breaks in the B2B catalog, not two products. 24-143 decks at 9.97, 144 and up at 8.97. Shopify's own plan-feature table lists quantity rules and quantity price breaks on Basic.
